title: Pointer Network Integration into Agent Workflows
summary: Five integration designs for embedding the pointer network into pre-task routing, live navigation, post-task learning, coordinator task assignment, and help-protocol resource matching.

1_pre_task_routing.title: Pre-Task Routing: Consult the Pointer Network Before Starting Work
1_pre_task_routing.problem: Agents currently start tasks without systematically discovering which SOPs, scripts, and sources are most relevant. They rely on manual knowledge or ad-hoc searching.

design.trigger: Agent receives a new task assignment (via coordinator_instructions or work_items table)

steps.detail: Map the task description to a known task category (e.g., 'data-gathering', 'stress-test', 'monitoring', 'wikipedia-enrichment'). Use keyword matching against pointer network node tags for ambiguous tasks.
steps.implementation: Parse current_task from agent_status or work_items.title. Normalize to a canonical task type string.

steps.detail: Call recommend_route(task, entry_node) to get historically best route if pattern data exists, or strength-based fallback from the pointer network.
steps.fallback: If no entry_node is known, the recommend function searches all SOP nodes for the best-connected one using tag overlap scoring (Fix #3/#4 in route_tracker.py).

steps.action: Build a ranked resource list from strength tiers
steps.detail: From the recommended route or entry node, collect all reachable nodes grouped by strength: primary (use first), supporting (use for orchestration), related (consider for scope extension). Ignore tangential unless exploring broadly.

Check that the recommended scripts/tools actually exist on disk. If a node in the pointer network references a file that has been moved or deleted, log a warning and fall back to the next-best strength tier.
steps.implementation: For each SCR/TOOL node, resolve its file_path from the scripts index.json. Verify existence with os.path.exists().

steps.detail: Begin recording the traversal path. Store the starting node and recommended route in the agent's session context so the post-task log captures the full journey.

design.integration_point_in_coordinator_hub: Add a 'route_plan' field to the coordinator_instructions payload. When the coordinator sends a task assignment, it includes the pre-computed recommended route as guidance.
design.integration_point_in_agent_reporter: Add an optional 'planned_route' parameter to AgentReporter.update_status() so agents can report which route they intend to follow. This enables the coordinator to detect deviations.

2_live_navigation.title: Live Navigation: Use the Network During Task Execution
2_live_navigation.problem: During execution, agents may hit blockers or discover that additional tools/data sources are needed. Currently there is no systematic way to dynamically discover related resources mid-task.

design.trigger: Agent encounters a blocker, needs additional data, or completes a sub-step and needs the next tool

mechanisms.description: Given the current node the agent is working with, query the pointer network for all outgoing edges. Filter by strength >= 'supporting' (weight >= 4). Present results sorted by weight descending.
mechanisms.use_case: Agent is using SCR-0036 and needs to find what other scripts work alongside it.
mechanisms.implementation: Load pointer-network.json, look up nodes[current_node].pointers, filter by strength in ('primary', 'supporting'), sort by weight desc.
mechanisms.pseudo_code: def get_adjacent(node_id, min_strength='supporting'): return sorted([p for p in pn['nodes'][node_id]['pointers'] if p['strength'] in allowed], key=lambda p: -p['weight'])

mechanisms.description: Find all nodes that point TO the current node. This answers: 'What SOPs or tools consider this resource important?'
mechanisms.use_case: Agent has a script but doesn't know which SOP governs its usage. Reverse lookup finds the parent SOP.
mechanisms.implementation: Scan all nodes for pointers where ptr['to'] == current_node. The pointer network already has 33 explicit backlink edges, but a full reverse index should be built at load time for O(1) lookups.
mechanisms.enhancement: Build a reverse_index dict at pointer network load time: {target_node: [{from: source_node, weight, strength}]}. Cache in memory for the session.

mechanisms.description: When the agent's current context doesn't match any known node, search the pointer network by tags. Each node has a 'tags' field (if populated) that enables fuzzy matching.
mechanisms.use_case: Agent needs 'wikipedia API' resources but doesn't know which node IDs are relevant. Search tags for 'wikipedia' or 'api' to find matching SRC/SCR nodes.
mechanisms.implementation: Build a tag_index at load time: {tag: [node_id, ...]}. Query with task keywords.

mechanisms.description: When the direct adjacency doesn't yield useful results, perform a 2-hop or 3-hop breadth-first search from the current node. Weight-based pruning keeps the search tractable: only follow edges with weight >= 3.
mechanisms.use_case: Agent needs to get from an SOP to a data source, but the SOP only points to scripts, which in turn point to sources. The 2-hop BFS discovers the transitive connection.
mechanisms.implementation: BFS with max_depth=3 and min_edge_weight=3. Return all reachable nodes with cumulative path weight.
mechanisms.complexity: With 310 nodes and avg ~15 pointers per node, a 3-hop BFS visits at most ~3375 paths (pruned). This is fast enough for real-time use.

session_context.description: Agents should maintain a lightweight navigation context during task execution.

fields.current_node: The pointer network node currently being used
fields.visited_nodes: Ordered list of all nodes visited so far (becomes the route log)
fields.deviation_notes: Why the agent deviated from the planned route, if applicable

3_post_task_learning.title: Post-Task Learning: Feed Results Back to Improve the Network
3_post_task_learning.problem: The pointer network is static. Route tracker logs usage, but there is no automated feedback loop that adjusts weights, adds new edges, or reclassifies strengths based on real-world outcomes.

design.trigger: Agent completes a task (outcome logged via route_tracker.py log)

feedback_mechanisms.description: After accumulating route data, adjust edge weights based on success/failure correlation.

rules.detail: If an edge appears in 5+ successful routes with a success rate > 80%, increase its weight by 1 (cap at 10).
rules.formula: new_weight = min(10, current_weight + 1) if success_rate > 0.8 and traversals >= 5

rules.detail: If an edge appears in 5+ routes with a success rate < 40%, decrease its weight by 1 (floor at 1).
rules.formula: new_weight = max(1, current_weight - 1) if success_rate < 0.4 and traversals >= 5

rules.detail: If an edge has 0 traversals across the last 50 logged routes, decrease its weight by 1. This surfaces dead connections that may need removal.

feedback_mechanisms.implementation: Run as a batch process: python3 route_tracker.py export, then a new 'optimize' command that applies weight adjustments to pointer-network.json.

feedback_mechanisms.description: Reclassify edge strength when weight crosses a tier boundary.

rules.demote_to_tangential: weight <= 1 AND traversals < 3 in last 50 routes

feedback_mechanisms.safety: Never auto-delete edges. Only reclassify. Human review (or coordinator review) needed for deletion.

feedback_mechanisms.description: When agents traverse node pairs that have no direct pointer, this is a 'discovered shortcut'. The system should propose new edges.
feedback_mechanisms.detection: In route logs, find consecutive hops (A -> B) where no direct pointer exists in the network from A to B. These are implicit multi-hop traversals that agents shortcutted.
feedback_mechanisms.action: Create a 'proposed_edges' list in route_analysis.json. Each proposed edge includes: source, target, traversal_count, success_rate, suggested_weight, suggested_strength. A coordinator or SOP-028 operator reviews and adds them.
feedback_mechanisms.auto_add_threshold: If a proposed edge has 10+ traversals with > 80% success rate, auto-add it with strength='related' and weight=3. This is conservative; human review can promote it.

feedback_mechanisms.description: When a task type consistently uses the same route with high success, codify it as a 'golden route' in route_patterns.json.
feedback_mechanisms.benefit: Golden routes become the default recommendation for that task type, bypassing the strength-based fallback entirely.

design.batch_schedule: Run the feedback loop after every multi-agent session, or when route_log.jsonl reaches 50+ new entries since last analysis.
design.new_cli_command: python3 route_tracker.py optimize --apply  (applies weight adjustments and strength reclassifications to pointer-network.json)

4_coordinator_integration.title: Coordinator Hub Integration: Pointer-Guided Task Assignment
4_coordinator_integration.problem: The coordinator_hub.py assigns tasks to agents without knowledge of which SOPs/scripts those agents will need. This can lead to suboptimal assignments where an agent is given a task far from its current pointer network context.

changes_to_coordinator_hub.change: Add a 'pointer_context' field to agent_status table
changes_to_coordinator_hub.schema_addition: ALTER TABLE agent_status ADD COLUMN pointer_context TEXT
changes_to_coordinator_hub.description: Stores JSON: {current_node, recent_nodes: [...], route_history_count}. Agents update this via AgentReporter when they traverse the pointer network.
changes_to_coordinator_hub.purpose: Lets the coordinator know which part of the pointer network an agent is currently working in.

changes_to_coordinator_hub.change: Add a pointer-aware task routing method to CoordinatorDashboard
changes_to_coordinator_hub.description: Given a task that maps to a known SOP entry node, find the agent whose pointer_context.current_node is closest to that SOP in the pointer network (fewest hops, highest cumulative weight).
algorithm: 1. Map the new task to its SOP entry node using route_tracker.recommend_route(task).
2. For each active agent, parse their pointer_context.current_node.
3. Compute graph distance from each agent's current_node to the task's SOP entry node using BFS on the pointer network (max 4 hops, weight >= 2).
4. Rank agents by: (a) shortest hop distance, (b) highest cumulative edge weight on the path, (c) agent's historical success rate for this task type (from route_patterns.json).
5. Assign to the top-ranked agent via send_instruction().
changes_to_coordinator_hub.fallback: If no agent has pointer_context set, or all agents are equidistant, fall back to current round-robin or load-based assignment.

changes_to_coordinator_hub.change: Enrich coordinator_instructions payload with route guidance
changes_to_coordinator_hub.description: When the coordinator sends a task instruction, include a 'recommended_route' field in the payload JSON.
Compare agents' actual pointer_context.recent_nodes against the recommended_route from their task instruction. Flag significant deviations (agent skipped primary tools or used tangential edges).
changes_to_coordinator_hub.action_on_deviation: Log a warning. Optionally send a 'route_suggestion' instruction to nudge the agent back to the recommended path. Never force — agents may have good reasons to deviate.

benefits: Agents are assigned tasks close to their current pointer network context, reducing ramp-up time.
Coordinators can proactively provide route guidance, reducing the agent's need for live navigation.
Deviation detection enables early intervention when an agent is struggling to find the right tools.

5_help_protocol_integration.title: Help Protocol Integration: Pointer-Based Resource and Agent Matching
5_help_protocol_integration.problem: When an agent requests help via help_protocol.py, matching is based solely on team_capabilities (string tags like 'coding', 'research'). The pointer network contains much richer information about which tools and SOPs are related, enabling more precise matching.

changes_to_help_protocol.change: Enrich help requests with pointer context
changes_to_help_protocol.description: When request_help() is called, auto-attach the requesting agent's current pointer_context (current_node, recent_nodes). This tells potential helpers exactly where in the pointer network the requesting agent is stuck.
changes_to_help_protocol.field_addition: Add 'pointer_context' column to help_requests table, storing JSON.

changes_to_help_protocol.description: Extend find_compatible_helpers() to score idle teams not just by capability match, but also by pointer network proximity.
algorithm: 1. Get the requesting agent's current_node from the help request's pointer_context.
2. For each idle team, get their agents' pointer_context.current_node from agent_status.
3. Compute pointer network distance from helper's current_node to requester's current_node (BFS, max 3 hops).
5. Return helpers sorted by combined score descending.

changes_to_help_protocol.description: When a help request is created, the system also queries the pointer network for resources that might resolve the blocker without needing another team's help.
algorithm: 1. From the requester's current_node, get all adjacent nodes with strength >= 'supporting'.
2. Filter to nodes the agent has NOT yet visited (from recent_nodes).
3. If any unvisited primary or supporting nodes exist, suggest them as 'self-help' resources before escalating to team help.
4. Include in help request response: {suggested_resources: [...], requires_team_help: true/false}
changes_to_help_protocol.benefit: Many help requests may be resolvable by pointing the agent to an adjacent resource they missed. This reduces unnecessary cross-team coordination.

changes_to_help_protocol.change: Route knowledge transfer in help acceptance
changes_to_help_protocol.description: When a helper team accepts a help request, include the requester's route history in the handoff. The helper can see which nodes the requester already tried and failed with, avoiding redundant work.
changes_to_help_protocol.implementation: When offer_help() succeeds, query route_log.jsonl for the requesting agent's recent routes for this task type. Include as 'prior_routes' in the work item assignment.

auto_assign_enhancement.description: Extend auto_assign_idle_teams() to use pointer proximity as a tiebreaker when multiple idle teams have equal capability match.
auto_assign_enhancement.implementation: After capability scoring, if two teams have equal match_score, prefer the team whose pointer_context.current_node is closer to the requester's current_node in the pointer network.

performance.pointer_network_caching: The pointer-network.json file is 854KB. Agents should load it once at session start and cache in memory. A file-modification-time check can trigger reloads if the network is updated mid-session.
performance.reverse_index: Build a reverse adjacency index at load time for O(1) backlink lookups. Current backlink count is only 33 explicit edges, but the reverse index covers all 4820 edges.
performance.tag_index: Build a tag-to-node-list index at load time for fast tag-based discovery.

consistency.write_locking: Pointer network weight adjustments (post-task learning) must use file-level locking or go through a single coordinator process to prevent concurrent write corruption.
consistency.eventual_consistency: Route recommendations are eventually consistent. An agent may get a recommendation based on slightly stale pattern data. This is acceptable since routes are guidance, not commands.

observability.route_deviation_metric: Track how often agents deviate from recommended routes. High deviation suggests the recommendations are poor or the pointer network is stale.
observability.self_help_success_rate: Track how often the 'suggest_resources_for_blocker' mechanism resolves help requests without team escalation. Target: > 30% self-resolution.
observability.feedback_loop_health: Monitor that the post-task learning loop is running. If route_log.jsonl grows by 50+ entries without an analyze/optimize cycle, alert.
